clinician.trajectory_summary: A 43-year-old male with a 20-pack-year smoking history presented with five months of left second toe pain, numbness, tingling, and burning sensation following ingrown toenail resection, with development of dry gangrene at the resection site. Initially diagnosed with mild PAD at an outside facility, he presented to vascular surgery clinic. CT angiography performed during the workup revealed a normal arterial system (ruling out significant PAD) but identified a 3.4 cm x 2.7 cm x 10.8 cm vascular malformation overlying the left fibularis muscles. Subsequent diagnostic angiography confirmed a large, complex AVM with feeding vessels from the anterior tibial, peroneal, and posterior tibial arteries. The patient was referred to interventional radiology for therapeutic embolization with polymerizing agent placement targeting the feeding branches.
